global: Forty years I have haggled in this market, and I still say a fair price is a gift to both parties, friend.
Four hundred pieces of silver for a horse? Ser, I would sooner walk to {town} on my own two feet.
My purse is lighter than my conscience this week, so I shall sell my spare mail and be done with it.
Trading honestly is the oldest oath in this land. Break it, and your name will rot long after your coin.
I shall give {gold} for that blade and not a copper more. Name your price, traveller, but name it wisely.
Grain in {town} has grown dear again. Heed my warning, ser, and buy your bread before the bells ring noon.
The merchant of {town} is a thief wearing a velvet cloak. Mark me, ser, I will not be robbed twice.
Gold alone does not build a house. Trust, ser, is the stone upon which every fair bargain is laid.
Pray tell, what do you ask for those boots, friend? I would sooner pay honestly than bargain in shadows.
Ah, the price of salt has made my old bones weary. In my youth, a single coin bought a whole cask.
